question: Does a recruiting class's top end win more than its depth?
answer: No. Point for point they are worth the same: CFB t = 0.70, CBB t = 0.51. The plain sum is not beaten.
findings: CFB, four classes on a roster: top 5 0.044 rating SD per 10 points, depth 0.027 (n=1,605).
CFB class sum over no class score: t = 3.49, 13/13 seasons. No reweighting passes (best t = -0.20).
CBB, returning and transfer value held fixed: top 2 0.071, depth 0.049 per 10 points (n=1,546).
CBB without the roster held fixed, depth reads -0.084: a deep class follows a thin returning roster.
method: Program rating z (opponent-adjusted margin in CFB, net rating in CBB) on the class's top-end and depth FV points, with the ratings before signing, a three-season baseline and program level as controls. Forms that reweight the class (split, decay, cap, star premium, power x decay) were pre-registered and scored held out by class or season, t clustered by program.
data: CFBD composite classes 2009-25 and cfbfastR results 2005-25; consensus-ranked CBB classes 2009-25 and program net ratings 2008-26. 1,605 CFB program-seasons, 1,546 CBB classes.
split_check: CFB NIL-era seasons: top 5 0.069, depth 0.006, t = 1.49 (n=511). Not distinguishable yet.
